whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the B2B Commerce Developer AP exam?

personas.label: Developers building custom storefronts
personas.description: You build Lightning Web Components and Apex for B2B stores and want to show that you know the supported ways to extend them.

personas.label: Integration engineers
personas.description: You connect B2B stores to ERPs and other services for pricing, stock, tax, and shipping.

personas.label: Technical consultants
personas.description: You advise clients on when to use B2B Commerce settings and when custom code is needed.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2B Commerce Developer AP exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This is a technical exam. Learn where B2B Commerce supports custom code, how storefront components work, and how to use the Commerce APIs. The questions go into detail.
bullets: About 68% to pass, or roughly 41 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current score.
Extension points: Learn how custom pricing, inventory, shipping, and tax connect to checkout.
Components and APIs: Expect questions about custom store components and Commerce APIs.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on experience building a custom B2B store component or integration helps. Aim for at least 80% on practice tests before booking.

examFormat.heading: B2B Commerce Developer AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions often describe a need that standard features do not meet, such as ERP pricing or a custom product page. Choose the supported way to build it.
bestWayToPass: Learn the extension points: Know how custom pricing, inventory, shipping, and tax connect to the store and checkout.
Build an LWC for a store: Learn how to expose it in Experience Builder and get data from Commerce APIs.
Know when not to code: If a standard setting meets the need, use it.
Study search and product data: Learn which fields are searchable and when to rebuild the index.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how to extend B2B Commerce with code, including custom storefront components, Apex integrations for pricing, stock, shipping, and tax, and Commerce APIs. The exam is 60 scored questions in 75 minutes, with a 68% pass mark, weighted towards Advanced Lightning Web Component Development (30%) and Basic Lightning Web Component Development (20%).

keyConcepts.h2: B2B Commerce Developer AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: LWC Commerce Components & Override Pattern
blocks.body: B2B stores use Lightning Web Components in Experience Builder. Add your own LWCs to store pages, or replace a standard component when it does not meet the need. To show a component in Experience Builder, expose it with the right targets in its metadata file and add any properties admins need. Commerce modules and wire adapters provide context such as the current product, cart, and buyer account. Use that context so the component shows data for the signed-in buyer. Keep components small and reuse standard features when possible.

blocks.heading: Commerce APIs & Storefront REST APIs
blocks.body: The **Commerce Connect REST APIs** let code and external apps work with products, carts, checkout, wishlists, and orders. Apex also has **ConnectApi** classes for server-side code. Use these APIs instead of directly reading or changing commerce records. They apply the buyer’s entitlements and prices. Headless and mobile apps can use the same APIs to support shopping outside the website.

blocks.heading: Checkout Integrations & Tax/Payment
blocks.body: Checkout can call external systems for **inventory**, **pricing**, **shipping**, and **tax**. Build an Apex class that implements the right integration interface or extension, then register it with the store. A **payment gateway adapter** connects to the payment provider so card details do not need to be stored in Salesforce. Handle slow and failed responses clearly, and test realistic carts as well as error cases.

blocks.heading: Search Configuration & Merchandising
blocks.body: Store search uses an index built from products, categories, and selected fields. Admins choose which fields are searchable and which can be used as filters. Developers can add product fields and mark them as searchable. After changing search settings or loading many products, **rebuild the index**. Rebuild large catalogs outside busy hours. Product data from integrations must include the fields used by search.

blocks.heading: Testing, Deployment & Performance
blocks.body: Apex code needs tests and at least 75% coverage for production deployment. Mock outside calls so tests do not depend on live systems. Store setup includes both metadata and records, so plan how to move catalogs, buyer groups, and settings between orgs. For performance, avoid heavy work in components loaded on every page, cache data that changes rarely, and keep integration calls fast. Slow pricing or tax calls make checkout slower.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass the B2B Commerce Developer AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions often describe a need that standard setup cannot meet. Choose a supported extension point instead of building a workaround.

blocks.heading: B2B Commerce Extensibility Framework
blocks.body: Use supported integration points for custom pricing, stock, shipping, and tax. Do not rebuild checkout from scratch.

blocks.heading: Storefront LWC Development
blocks.body: Expose LWCs to Experience Builder in the metadata file. Get store context from Commerce modules instead of hard-coding IDs.

blocks.heading: Apex Extension Points
blocks.body: Use ConnectApi commerce classes in Apex so buyer entitlements and prices are applied.

blocks.heading: External Catalog Integration
blocks.body: Load outside products using external IDs, then rebuild the search index.

blocks.heading: Order Fulfillment Integration
blocks.body: Send placed orders to the ERP with events or asynchronous Apex. Keep order status in sync.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after B2B Commerce Developer:

sampleQuestions.question: Prices must come from the company’s ERP when a buyer adds a product to the cart. What should the developer do?
options: Build and register an Apex pricing integration
Change the store theme
Ask buyers to call for prices
Copy the ERP prices into each product description
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2B Commerce supports custom pricing integrations that can get a price from the ERP when needed.
whyWrong: Calling for each price defeats online checkout.
A price in the description cannot be used by the cart.

sampleQuestions.question: A developer wants admins to drag a custom LWC onto store pages in Experience Builder. What must they do?
options: Add it to a record page layout
Expose the component and set Experience Builder targets in its metadata
Rewrite it in Visualforce
Deploy it only as a static resource and reference it from the store's head markup
sampleQuestions.explanation: Expose the LWC and add the needed targets in its js-meta.xml file so it appears in Experience Builder.
whyWrong: Record page layouts are not how admins add components to store pages.
Visualforce is not needed to build a store LWC.
A static resource is not a Lightning component.

sampleQuestions.question: Apex must add a product to a buyer’s cart while applying their entitlements and prices. What should it use?
options: Insert a CartItem record directly with DML
Send an outbound message
Use the ConnectApi Commerce classes
Query Product2 with SOQL
sampleQuestions.explanation: ConnectApi Commerce methods apply the buyer’s entitlements and pricing. Direct DML would skip those rules.
whyWrong: Direct DML skips Commerce rules and can create an invalid cart.
Outbound messages send data out of Salesforce.
A query reads records; it does not add an item to the cart.

sampleQuestions.question: Checkout must calculate tax using an outside tax service. What should the developer build?
options: Create a report that shows tax
Add a validation rule
Add a formula field to the cart that multiplies by a fixed rate
Register an Apex tax integration with the store
sampleQuestions.explanation: Checkout supports a tax integration. A registered Apex class can call the service and return tax amounts.
whyWrong: Reports show information after checkout.
A validation rule checks data; it does not calculate tax.
A formula field cannot call an outside service.

sampleQuestions.question: Card payments must use a payment provider without storing card numbers in Salesforce. What should be used?
options: A payment gateway adapter for the provider
A custom encrypted field for card numbers on the Order
Email card details to finance
A long text field on the Order
sampleQuestions.explanation: A payment gateway adapter connects checkout to the provider, which handles the card information and returns a result.
whyWrong: Storing card numbers in Salesforce fields creates a security risk.
Email is not a safe way to send card details.
A long text field still stores sensitive card details.

sampleQuestions.question: A custom product field must be searchable in the store. The developer created the field. What else is needed?
options: Copy the value into the product name
Mark it searchable in search settings, then rebuild the index
Add the field to the buyer’s profile
Nothing; every custom field is searched automatically once created
sampleQuestions.explanation: Choose the field in search settings and rebuild the index so it includes the field.
whyWrong: Changing product names is a workaround that can harm data quality.
Profiles do not control store search.
Only selected fields are indexed.

sampleQuestions.question: A pricing integration can take 20 seconds and slows checkout. What should the developer do first?
options: Remove pricing from checkout and show buyers the final amount later by email, once the ERP has responded
Retry the call ten times
Set a timeout and clear fallback message, then work with the ERP team to improve response time
Ask buyers to wait
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use a timeout and a clear fallback message, and work with the ERP team to improve the slow service.
whyWrong: Removing pricing prevents buyers from placing correct orders.
Repeated retries can make checkout take even longer.
Asking buyers to wait can lead them to abandon the cart.

sampleQuestions.question: A mobile app must let buyers browse products and manage a cart using the website’s rules. What should it use?
options: Take screenshots of the website
Run SOQL directly from the app
Use a nightly CSV file
Use the B2B Commerce REST APIs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Commerce REST APIs give the app access to the store’s products, prices, and cart logic.
whyWrong: Screen scraping is fragile and breaks when the website changes.
Mobile apps should not query Salesforce directly with SOQL; that can also bypass Commerce rules.
A nightly CSV cannot manage a live cart.

sampleQuestions.question: Tests for a shipping integration fail when the provider is unavailable. What should the developer change?
options: Use HttpCalloutMock so tests do not call the live service
Lower the coverage target so the failing tests no longer block it
Run tests only at night
Remove the tests
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mock callouts let tests run the integration code without depending on the outside service.
whyWrong: Coverage requirements do not change because the provider is down.
The provider could also be unavailable at night.
Removing tests can prevent Apex from being deployed to production.

sampleQuestions.question: A product comparison feature is not available as a standard component. What should the developer do?
options: Use a Visualforce page in the store
Build a custom LWC and add it to product pages in Experience Builder
Edit the source of Salesforce’s standard component and redeploy it to the store
Ask buyers to open two browser tabs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom LWCs are a supported way to add features to store pages.
whyWrong: Visualforce is not the preferred way to extend modern store pages.
Salesforce’s standard component source cannot be edited.
Opening two tabs does not provide a comparison feature.

sampleQuestions.question: 10,000 products load from the ERP each night, but new items take days to appear in search. What should the team do?
options: Load each product one at a time throughout the night
Turn off search
Rebuild the search index after each nightly load
Shorten product names
sampleQuestions.explanation: Rebuild the search index after the nightly load so new products appear in search.
whyWrong: Loading one at a time does not update the search index.
Turning off search would make products harder to find.
Product name length is not the cause.

sampleQuestions.question: An order must reach the ERP after checkout without slowing the buyer down. What approach fits?
options: Ask sales reps to re-enter the order
Make a synchronous call to the ERP before saving the order, and wait
Export orders manually each night
Publish an event or start asynchronous Apex after order creation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Asynchronous processing sends the order in the background so the buyer does not have to wait.
whyWrong: Re-entering orders is slow and can cause errors.
A synchronous call makes checkout wait and can fail if the ERP is down.
A nightly export delays order processing.

sampleQuestions.question: A store component must show data for the logged-in buyer’s account. How should it get the account?
options: Use Commerce context for the current buyer
Read a shared custom setting
Ask the buyer to enter an account number each visit
Hard-code an account ID
sampleQuestions.explanation: Commerce context modules provide the current buyer account, cart, and store at runtime.
whyWrong: A shared setting would not give the current buyer’s account.
Buyers should not need to type their account number.
A hard-coded ID could show the same account to every buyer.

sampleQuestions.question: Before deploying a custom inventory integration, what must the Apex code include?
options: A managed package
Test classes with at least 75% code coverage
A Visualforce page
A Full sandbox refresh completed in the last 24 hours
sampleQuestions.explanation: Apex needs test classes and at least 75% code coverage for production deployment.
whyWrong: A managed package is not required for every custom class.
A Visualforce page is not required.
A sandbox refresh is not a deployment requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: A requirement can be met with standard checkout settings or custom code. What should the developer recommend?
options: Always write custom code
Build checkout outside Salesforce
Use the standard configuration
Ignore the requirement
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use configuration when it meets the need. Use custom code only when configuration cannot meet it.
whyWrong: Custom code adds maintenance and upgrade work when it is not needed.
A separate checkout loses built-in Commerce rules.
The team still needs to meet the requirement.
